claude.sample_unit: AI-generated summary sections rated (784 ratings across four rater models)

links.outcome: Agreement among LLM raters using same rubric on summary error density
links.effect: Measured error density varied about 4-fold among raters, 0.150 to 0.557 errors per 100 words (Friedman p < 0.001); human check on ten articles agreed only with Claude Sonnet 4.6.
links.quote: Across the 784 ratings, the measured error density varied by about a factor of 4 among raters, ranging from 0.150 to 0.557 errors per 100 words (Friedman test, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Omission of source safety warnings in AI summaries as detected by different raters
links.effect: Of 28 sections with a source safety warning, warning missing in 22 per strictest rater vs 4 per most lenient; lenient raters identified only 3 and 2 of 9 safety omissions.
links.quote: Of the 28 sections that had a safety warning in their source, the warning was missing in 22 cases according to the strictest rater and in 4 cases according to the most lenient rater.

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs as raters of AI-generated summaries with a source-anchored rubric and cross-validating against human raters

screen.reason: Empirical study testing whether LLMs can reliably act as automated evaluators/raters (guardrails/checks) for patient-facing biomedical summaries, specifically assessing safety warning omission detection compared to human review.
